Taiwan chipmakers are simultaneously hedging their geographic exposure — broadening investment toward Europe, Japan, and ASEAN in response to potential US semiconductor tariffs — **complicating multi-year capacity planning** for equipment buyers who need stable demand signals to commit to tool orders.

briefs.headline: US firms commit $2 billion to South Korean semiconductor supply chains
briefs.paragraph: Four US technology companies — Air Products, **Axcelis**, Corning, and Pacifico Energy — have committed a combined **$2 billion** in investments across South Korea's semiconductor materials, equipment, and clean-energy sectors. The move targets supply-chain resilience between the two countries and feeds into Seoul's three strategic Mega Project programs. Axcelis's participation is notable given its ion-implant equipment business; Corning supplies specialty glass substrates. The announcement follows Seoul's push last week for tariff carve-outs as Washington prepares a new semiconductor levy structure.

briefs.headline: Silicon photonics team targets 1.6T DR8 by year-end, 3.2T links next
briefs.paragraph: A cross-border team comprising Taiwan's Ligitek Electronics, Liverage Technology, research institute **ITRI** (Industrial Technology Research Institute), and Dutch packaging specialist Phix is targeting 1.6T DR8 silicon photonics modules by end of 2026, with **3.2T optical links** slated as the follow-on milestone. The program reflects AI data-center pressure to move from copper to optical interconnects inside the package — a trend that also feeds demand for InP wafer capacity and co-packaged optics test infrastructure covered in prior issues.

briefs.headline: India launches Semicon 2.0 pitching itself as global chip redundancy to Taiwan
briefs.paragraph: India unveiled the next phase of its semiconductor policy — **Semicon 2.0** — and senior officials traveled to Taipei to frame the program explicitly as supply-chain redundancy for an over-concentrated global industry rather than import substitution. The pitch targeted Taiwanese materials, gas, equipment, and packaging firms whose customers are already asking them to establish a second production base. A South Korean-Indian joint venture also completed a photoresist materials plant targeting a China-free supply chain, adding a materials dimension to the policy push.

briefs.headline: KAIST and Samsung develop entropy-stabilized catalyst to destroy fab greenhouse gases
briefs.paragraph: Researchers at **KAIST** and Samsung Electronics have developed a new catalyst based on entropy stabilization — mixing multiple metal atoms to disorder the crystal lattice and thereby lock the active sites in place — to decompose perfluorocarbon (PFC) gases used in semiconductor etch and cleaning processes. PFCs carry a global warming potential **6,000 times that of CO₂** and are among the hardest fab (chip factory) emissions to treat. The entropy-stabilized structure extends catalyst lifetime significantly compared to conventional single-metal designs, potentially reducing both the operating cost and environmental footprint of high-volume fabs.

email_subject: High-NA EUV enters volume production; TSMC and Samsung commit to 12-inch masks; ASML breaks ground on Eindhoven campus
intro: Three major announcements at this week's SPIE Photomask conference mark a turning point for High-NA EUV lithography — Intel is already running it in production, and TSMC and Samsung have now set timelines for their own deployments.

lead_brief.headline: Intel crosses one million High-NA EUV wafers; TSMC and Samsung set deployment timelines
lead_brief.paragraph: **ASML** and Intel Foundry announced at the SPIE Photomask Technology and EUV Lithography conference that Intel has processed more than one million wafers using High-NA EUV — the next-generation lithography (chip-printing optical process) platform that raises the lens numerical aperture from 0.33 on current NXE scanners to 0.55 on the new EXE systems. Higher NA lets the optics collect more diffracted light from the mask, tightening the minimum printable pitch and reducing the need for multiple-patterning — the costly technique of splitting a single circuit layer across several sequential exposures. Intel reports that overlay (layer-to-layer alignment accuracy, measured in nanometers), throughput, and tool availability are all meeting production expectations, and that High-NA-patterned layers on its 18A process match or outperform equivalent layers done on 0.33-NA EUV scanners. Select layers of the Panther Lake processor (Core Ultra Series 3) are already patterned this way. The field-size constraint of High-NA optics — anamorphic imaging shrinks the exposed area relative to a full-field EUV scanner — is being managed today through chip floor-planning and reticle stitching, supported by Intel's process design kit. Looking further out, **TSMC committed to High-NA high-volume manufacturing by 2030**, and Samsung announced it will introduce High-NA into DRAM production by 2028 — the first memory maker to do so. All three chipmakers have also backed a joint ASML-TSMC initiative to transition from the industry's decades-old 6-inch photomask format to a 12-inch format by 2033, which is projected to boost scanner productivity by roughly 40 percent and eliminate the stitching constraints inherent to today's smaller masks.

briefs.headline: ASML breaks ground on second Eindhoven campus to support growth
briefs.paragraph: **ASML** held a groundbreaking ceremony at Brainport Industries Campus North in Eindhoven on September 8, attended by Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten. The new campus is planned to span roughly 350,000 square meters and could eventually accommodate up to 20,000 workplaces across multiple construction phases. The expansion is designed to add manufacturing capacity in the Netherlands as global demand for lithography equipment continues to grow, keeping key operations concentrated in the Brainport region alongside ASML's existing Veldhoven facilities.

briefs.headline: Samsung shifts more than half its 4nm capacity to HBM4 base dies
briefs.paragraph: **Samsung Electronics** is directing 50–60% of its 4nm foundry (chip-for-hire factory) capacity to base dies for sixth-generation HBM4 (high-bandwidth memory — stacked DRAM die connected by through-silicon vias) as of August, accelerating shipments to AI chip customers. Separately, Samsung is also speeding its silicon photonics development by adopting the same wafer-level test equipment suppliers that TSMC (Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, world's largest foundry) uses, targeting completion of photonic integrated circuit testing this year ahead of planned silicon photonics foundry services in 2027.

briefs.headline: US-Korea chip tariff talks intensify as Samsung and SK Hynix weigh US investment
briefs.paragraph: Bilateral US-Korea semiconductor investment negotiations have intensified, with chip tariff policy now directly shaping the US expansion decisions of **Samsung Electronics** and SK Hynix. SK Hynix broke ground on its HBM advanced packaging facility in West Lafayette, Indiana, in late August. The broader question — whether Korean chipmakers' US investment commitments will earn tariff relief — remains unresolved, as the first project under South Korea's $200 billion strategic-investment mechanism **approaches final selection**.

briefs.headline: Huawei's Kirin 9050 Pro claims 55% density gain without a new process node
briefs.paragraph: **Huawei**'s Kirin 9050 Pro is the first commercial chip to deploy its LogicFolding architecture under the company's Tau Scaling Law, claiming **55% higher transistor density** at the same process node alongside power reductions of 66%, 58%, and 41% for its NPU, GPU, and CPU performance cores respectively. The approach targets density gains through design and layout techniques rather than moving to a more advanced lithography node — a path Huawei has pursued as export controls limit its access to leading-edge equipment.

briefs.headline: SK Hynix weighs parallel Gwangju cluster investment alongside Yongin build
briefs.paragraph: **SK Hynix** is considering investing in South Korea's planned Gwangju semiconductor cluster concurrently with its ongoing Yongin fab (chip factory) buildout, rather than sequencing the two projects. The potential overlap is significant for equipment suppliers: the key question is whether Gwangju would generate incremental equipment orders or simply pull spending forward from later Yongin phases. A decision has not been announced, but the discussion signals that SK Hynix's domestic capacity expansion may be broader than previously understood.

briefs.headline: ASM International nominates former Infineon COO to supervisory board
briefs.paragraph: **ASM International** plans to nominate Rutger Wijburg to its supervisory board, with a shareholder vote expected at an extraordinary general meeting in early March 2027. Wijburg served as COO and management board member at Infineon from 2022 to 2025 and previously held senior roles at Globalfoundries, NXP, and Philips Semiconductors. He currently sits on the supervisory boards of Zeiss and Smart Photonics, giving him visibility into both metrology (precision in-line measurement) and photonics — areas of direct relevance to ASM's deposition equipment business.

briefs.headline: Tungsten hexafluoride supply tightens as memory capacity race accelerates
briefs.paragraph: Surging memory fab (chip factory) construction across South Korea, the US, and China is driving sharp demand growth for **tungsten hexafluoride** (WF6 — a specialty gas used in tungsten deposition for chip interconnects), while China's export controls on tungsten powder have simultaneously pushed raw-material prices higher. The combination is drawing attention to a supply chain that rarely makes headlines: WF6 is a critical process chemical for DRAM and NAND manufacturing, and **capacity constraints** could create a bottleneck if fab buildout continues at its current pace.

briefs.headline: Co-packaged optics testing hurdles span all four insertion stages through 2027
briefs.paragraph: **Co-packaged optics** (CPO — optical interconnects integrated directly into the chip package) has entered mass production deployment, but yield-protecting test processes face distinct challenges at each of its four integration stages (Insertions 1 through 4). Full 100% wafer-level testing is expected to accelerate in 2027 as the industry works through those barriers — an update to the earlier shift toward mid-stage testing reported last week, confirming that the test challenge extends across the entire CPO assembly sequence.

email_subject: Samsung and TSMC lock in High-NA EUV timelines; CHIPS Act quantum awards finalized; Amkor Arizona hits $12B
intro: High-NA EUV adoption crystallized this week, with Samsung, TSMC, and imec all publishing concrete plans. The CHIPS Act quantum program also moved from letters of intent to signed contracts.

lead_brief.headline: Samsung targets 2028 High-NA DRAM debut as TSMC sets 2030 logic entry
lead_brief.paragraph: **Samsung Electronics** and ASML announced plans to deploy High-NA EUV lithography (next-gen EUV, higher numerical aperture) in high-volume DRAM (dynamic random-access memory) manufacturing by 2028, making Samsung the first memory maker to commit to the technology. TSMC separately disclosed it will introduce High-NA into logic production around 2030, targeting its A10 or A11 process nodes, and will co-develop a larger-format EUV photomask with ASML for those scanners. The photomask transition matters because High-NA tools use a 0.55 NA objective lens — up from 0.33 NA in current EUV scanners — which narrows the minimum printable half-pitch roughly in proportion to the NA increase, but also shrinks the image field on the wafer, requiring either smaller dies or a new, larger reticle format to recover throughput. Separately, imec reported at SPIE that conventional chemically amplified resists (CAR — photosensitive polymers that amplify exposure by catalytic chain reactions) can pattern line-and-space features down to 22 nm pitch and vias at 28 nm center-to-center under High-NA EUV, a result that extends proven resist chemistry into the High-NA era and reduces process risk for both Samsung and TSMC as they finalize insertion plans. With Intel already running small-scale High-NA production, all major chipmakers have now publicly committed to the platform.

briefs.headline: CHIPS Act finalizes $775 million in quantum computing awards with equity stakes
briefs.paragraph: The US Department of Commerce signed binding CHIPS and Science Act awards with five companies, converting May's letters of intent into contracts. **GlobalFoundries** receives up to $375 million — the largest share — to build a domestic quantum foundry (chip-for-hire factory) serving multiple qubit architectures, with capabilities spanning cryogenic CMOS process design kits, advanced packaging, and heterogeneous integration. Rigetti, D-Wave, PsiQuantum, and Quantinuum each receive up to $100 million spread across superconducting, photonic, and trapped-ion approaches. Each award carries **a minority government equity stake** as a condition of funding.

briefs.headline: Huawei coordinates China's domestic DUV lithography push through SMIC trials
briefs.paragraph: **Huawei** is acting as a central organizer for China's domestic deep ultraviolet lithography (DUV — older 193 nm chip-printing tools) ecosystem, backing Shanghai-based Yuliangsheng — a spinout of SiCarrier, itself linked to Huawei — and helping connect it to major fabs including SMIC. Yuliangsheng's machines are being tested on Huawei's own production lines and at SMIC, starting with less complex chips before targeting AI silicon. The effort represents **China's most coordinated DUV localization push** yet, aimed at reducing exposure to ASML export restrictions.

briefs.headline: Amkor doubles Arizona packaging campus to $12 billion after customer demand surges
briefs.paragraph: **Amkor Technology** will add a second phase to its advanced packaging and test campus in Chandler, Arizona after customer commitments exceeded the cleanroom space planned for phase 1. The expansion adds 60,000 square meters of cleanroom, bringing the campus to roughly 93,000 square meters total, and lifts the project's planned investment **to approximately $12 billion**. The site offers wafer bump, probe, assembly, and test capabilities and is expected to employ more than 3,500 workers once both phases are complete.

briefs.headline: Imec demonstrates world-first three-level NbTiN superconducting circuits at 30nm wiring
briefs.paragraph: At the 2026 Applied Superconductivity Conference, **imec** (Belgian R&D hub for chipmaking) reported two firsts in superconducting processor fabrication: a three-metal-level niobium-titanium-nitride (NbTiN) Josephson junction circuit reaching **3.8 million junctions per square centimeter**, and superconducting routing wires scaled to 30 nm linewidth — the finest demonstrated for superconducting digital logic. Josephson junctions switch via quantum tunneling rather than transistor action, making them far faster and more energy-efficient than silicon CMOS at scale, though cryogenic cooling remains a prerequisite that currently limits the technology to large-scale computing applications.

briefs.headline: Samsung opens $257 million Yokohama packaging lab to close HBM gap with SK Hynix
briefs.paragraph: **Samsung Electronics** opened an advanced packaging research center in Yokohama — the Samsung Advanced Package Lab — with total investment of roughly JPY 40 billion (approximately $257 million), including JPY 22.5 billion in Japanese government support. The 6,600-square-meter facility, attended by 15 major Japanese suppliers including Tokyo Electron and Ibiden, lets Samsung and its partners evaluate HBM (high-bandwidth memory — stacked DRAM die connected by through-silicon vias) materials and develop prototypes locally rather than shipping samples to South Korea, **cutting evaluation cycles by up to two months**.

briefs.headline: China hits Japanese dichlorosilane with up to 99.2% anti-dumping duties
briefs.paragraph: China's Ministry of Commerce has imposed provisional anti-dumping tariffs of 80.8% to **99.2%** on Japanese dichlorosilane (DCS — a specialty gas used to deposit silicon nitride, silicon oxide, and polysilicon films in chip fabs). Starting September 8, importers must lodge deposits at those rates with Chinese customs. DCS is a front-end deposition feedstock used across logic, memory, and analog manufacturing; Japanese suppliers held roughly 60% of China's DCS market in the first half of 2025, down from 80% in 2022 as domestic Chinese suppliers gained ground.

briefs.headline: Axcelis plans $35 million South Korea equipment manufacturing facility
briefs.paragraph: **Axcelis Technologies**, the Beverly, Massachusetts-based ion implantation equipment maker, will invest $35 million in a new manufacturing facility in Pyeongtaek, Gyeonggi Province, South Korea. The roughly 200,000-square-foot plant will include Class 1,000 and Class 10,000 cleanrooms, warehousing, and a training center. Ion implanters precisely dose silicon wafers (silicon discs chips are made on) with dopant atoms to set transistor electrical properties; the move expands Axcelis's in-region capacity as **Korean memory fabs accelerate**.

briefs.headline: CXMT captures 10% of global DRAM revenue, pressuring South Korea's work-hour rules
briefs.paragraph: **CXMT** (ChangXin Memory Technologies, China's fourth-largest DRAM maker) reached 10% of global DRAM revenue in Q2 2026, up from 4% a year earlier, per Counterpoint Research data. Samsung held 38% and SK Hynix 25%, with the two South Korean firms' combined share falling from 72% to 63% year-over-year. The gains have reignited a domestic debate in South Korea over its 52-hour workweek cap, with semiconductor engineers arguing that **advanced R&D cannot be constrained** by fixed-schedule rules as China's memory capabilities close in.

email_subject: ASML and chipmakers push larger High-NA masks; TSMC August revenue +53%; OpenAI eyes Samsung for AI chips
intro: The High-NA EUV photomask format debate dominated this week's SPIE proceedings, as all four leading chipmakers aligned behind a larger reticle standard that could take years to qualify. TSMC's August revenue data and OpenAI's Samsung sourcing news round out a busy week.

lead_brief.headline: Industry unifies behind larger High-NA EUV photomask but warns transition will take years
lead_brief.paragraph: **ASML**, Intel, Samsung, and TSMC have formally aligned behind a move to 6×12-inch photomasks (the glass plates that carry circuit patterns for optical printing) for High-NA EUV lithography (next-gen EUV, higher numerical aperture), up from the current 6×6-inch standard used with conventional EUV tools. The larger format matters because High-NA EUV's increased numerical aperture narrows the field of view each exposure can cover — a smaller printable area per shot means large processor dies either require costly multi-exposure stitching or a physically bigger mask to maintain acceptable throughput. Moving to 6×12 inches would restore single-exposure coverage for large dies, avoiding the overlay (layer-to-layer alignment, measured in nanometers) errors that stitching seams introduce. The challenge is that the entire mask supply chain — pellicle (thin membrane protecting the mask from particles) materials, inspection tools, handling robotics, and actinic (EUV-wavelength) review systems — must be re-engineered for the new format. All four companies backing the initiative signals industry consensus, but the article notes the transition **may take years** before high-volume fabs can rely on it. This story continues last week's reporting on Intel's one-million-wafer High-NA milestone and the Samsung–ASML collaboration deepening around 2028 DRAM deployment.

briefs.headline: ASML partners with Xanadu to reduce optical losses in photonic quantum chips
briefs.paragraph: **ASML** is collaborating with Canadian quantum computing company Xanadu to study how advanced lithography can cut optical losses in photonic quantum processors. The focus is on pattern fidelity and line edge roughness — surface irregularities at waveguide sidewalls scatter photons and reduce coherence, a fundamental barrier to fault-tolerant photonic quantum computing. Better lithographic patterning would smooth those interfaces and reduce scattering loss. The partnership will evaluate which lithography approaches best enable the low-loss structures Xanadu needs before committing to **high-volume manufacturing**.

briefs.headline: TSMC August revenue hits $16.3 billion, up 53% year over year
briefs.paragraph: **TSMC** (Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, world's largest foundry — chip-for-hire factory) reported August 2026 consolidated revenue of NT$514.81 billion, roughly US$16.3 billion, up 53.3% from a year earlier and 10.1% from July. Year-to-date revenue through August reached NT$3.387 trillion, a **39.3% year-over-year increase**, with AI chip demand the primary driver. The figures track with broader equipment and packaging data showing sustained fab utilization pressure across leading nodes.

briefs.headline: OpenAI explores Samsung as a second foundry source for AI processors
briefs.paragraph: **OpenAI** is in discussions to have its next-generation AI accelerators manufactured at Samsung, potentially alongside its existing relationship with TSMC. Double-sourcing across two foundries (chip-for-hire factories) would give OpenAI supply redundancy and additional wafer capacity as its in-house silicon ambitions grow. Samsung's 4nm capacity — already more than half committed to HBM4 base dies, as reported last week — would need to absorb another major customer, **adding pressure** on an already constrained advanced-node schedule.

briefs.headline: GlobalFoundries and Quantinuum finalize CHIPS Act quantum R&D awards
briefs.paragraph: Two more CHIPS and Science Act quantum awards have converted to final agreements. **GlobalFoundries** closed a $375 million R&D award tied to milestone achievements over five years for its Quantum Technology Solutions business. Separately, Quantinuum finalized a $100 million award, partnering with GlobalFoundries to fabricate next-generation ion traps and control electronics, and with Monarch Quantum on lasers and optical components. Both deals continue the wave of CHIPS quantum awards **finalized this week**, following last week's five-company signing.

briefs.headline: Spirox brings nonlinear optical inspection to through-glass via metrology
briefs.paragraph: **Spirox** has entered the advanced packaging inspection market using nonlinear optical technology to image through-glass vias (TGVs — vertical conductors drilled through glass substrates). Chairman Peter Chin said the system can scan an entire substrate in 20 minutes, with aperture sizes at 4 µm currently qualified and 3 µm still under validation. As glass core substrates transition from development to mass production, **whole-substrate scanning speed** is emerging as a key differentiator for TGV metrology tools alongside TSV (through-silicon via) inspection.

briefs.headline: CXMT's HBM3 yield stuck near 25% as TSV stacking proves difficult
briefs.paragraph: Building on last week's report that **CXMT** (ChangXin Memory Technologies, China's fourth-largest DRAM maker) reached 10% of global DRAM revenue, a new challenge has surfaced: the company's HBM3 (high-bandwidth memory — stacked DRAM with through-silicon vias) trial production is reportedly yielding around 25%. TSV (through-silicon via — vertical copper connections linking stacked dies) formation and precision die stacking demand tighter process control than planar DRAM, and **low yield** at this stage suggests CXMT's AI memory ramp remains well behind its conventional DRAM progress.

briefs.headline: STMicroelectronics targets $2 billion in AI data-center revenue by 2027
briefs.paragraph: **STMicroelectronics** told investors in New York that it expects more than US$2 billion in AI data-center revenue in 2027, with roughly 80% of that figure coming from fiber-optic data transmission chips. The disclosure is the first time the company has broken out the product mix behind its AI outlook after raising its forecast in July. The heavy weighting toward fiber chips — rather than compute silicon — positions ST as a **photonics component supplier** to the data-center buildout rather than a logic foundry competitor.

briefs.headline: Sub-2nm manufacturing blurs process boundaries as tolerances reach atomic scale
briefs.paragraph: A detailed review in **Semiconductor Engineering** finds that below the 2nm node (manufacturing generation), formerly discrete fabrication steps are merging because process margins have shrunk to single-atom dimensions. A single misplaced atom can shift device behavior, a gentle probe tip can rupture a thin oxide, and a nanometer-scale particle left from a sacrificial etch step can scrap an entire multi-die stack. Metrology (precision in-line measurement) faces a related problem: process variation at this scale can trigger **false error signals** in measurement tools themselves, complicating the feedback loops that process control relies on.

email_subject: SK Hynix joins 12-inch High-NA mask push; WFE hits $270B forecast; SMIC closes on Samsung
intro: The High-NA EUV photomask story keeps growing: SK Hynix has joined the coalition targeting 12-inch masks, while new forecasts put wafer fab equipment spending at $270 billion by 2030 on AI-driven demand.

lead_brief.headline: SK Hynix joins 12-inch High-NA EUV mask initiative targeting 2031 pilot line
lead_brief.paragraph: The 12-inch High-NA EUV photomask initiative — reported here last week when ASML, TSMC, Intel, and Samsung aligned behind it — has added two more members. **SK Hynix** is now considering joining the coalition, and NY Creates (the New York state semiconductor R&D organization) has formally signed on. The expanded group is targeting a 12-inch mask pilot line by 2031 and production-ready systems by 2033. To understand the stakes: today's High-NA EUV scanners use 6-inch reticles (the glass plates carrying circuit patterns). Doubling the mask area to 12 inches increases the printable field on each exposure, easing the stitching constraints that arise when very large chip dies must be assembled from multiple smaller exposures, and improving scanner throughput. SK Hynix is separately targeting 2028 to insert High-NA EUV into DRAM mass production, matching Samsung's previously announced timeline. Imec's demonstration of **single-exposure 22nm-pitch patterning** using established chemically amplified resist — cited at the same SPIE conference — meanwhile confirms that the resist infrastructure for early High-NA production layers is already in place, removing one key readiness concern.

briefs.headline: WFE spending forecast to reach $270 billion by 2030 on AI data-center demand
briefs.paragraph: **Futurum Group** projects global wafer fab equipment (WFE — tools used to build chips in a fab) spending will reach roughly **$270 billion by 2030**, driven by AI data-center expansion. The firm's estimate links physical infrastructure to silicon demand directly: 1 gigawatt of AI compute capacity requires approximately 745,000 wafers and $6.1 billion in WFE investment, giving a concrete ratio between power capacity buildout and equipment orders. Advanced logic, HBM, DRAM, and advanced packaging capacity are all cited as demand drivers.

briefs.headline: Taiwan AI supply chain posts 76% revenue surge in August filings
briefs.paragraph: Taiwan-listed companies across the AI server supply chain reported combined August revenue of NT$2.84 trillion (roughly US$89.7 billion), up 76.5% year over year and 9.9% from July, based on filings to Taiwan's stock exchange. Within the rack-level segment, rail kits led with **191% year-over-year growth**, thermal management rose 58%, and power supplies 33% — a pattern suggesting rack-scale deployment, not just component ordering, is the binding constraint driving demand upstream into wafer and packaging equipment.

briefs.headline: SMIC narrows foundry market gap with Samsung as global revenue hits record
briefs.paragraph: Global top-10 foundry (chip-for-hire factory) revenue reached a record **$53.49 billion** in Q2 2026, up 11.5% quarter over quarter, according to TrendForce. **SMIC** posted the strongest growth among the top three, with revenue rising 20% sequentially to more than $3 billion and market share edging to 5.4%, closing in on Samsung Foundry at 5.9%. The gap between China's leading foundry and Samsung's logic-for-hire business is now less than half a percentage point — a shift driven largely by domestic Chinese chip demand redirected away from foreign suppliers.

briefs.headline: Biren posts 2,000% revenue growth as US export controls vacate China AI chip market
briefs.paragraph: **Biren Technology**, China's domestic AI accelerator designer, posted roughly **2,000% year-over-year revenue growth** in the first half of 2026, according to Tom's Hardware, as Nvidia and AMD GPUs became effectively unavailable in China following successive rounds of US export controls. The figure reflects both genuine demand growth and an almost complete removal of foreign competition rather than a technology breakthrough, but the scale of the displacement illustrates how controls have restructured the China AI chip market and concentrated equipment and wafer demand at domestic fabs.

briefs.headline: Samsung 2nm gains design-tool validation as Synopsys cuts NPU die area 22%
briefs.paragraph: **Synopsys** has demonstrated a 22% reduction in die area for a neural processing unit implemented with its Fusion Compiler electronic design automation tool on Samsung Foundry's SF2P 2nm process. The result provides a concrete, design-level data point for customers evaluating Samsung's 2nm node (manufacturing generation) against rival offerings — a market where TSMC's comparable process has attracted the bulk of early commitments. Die area reduction at equivalent performance directly affects cost per chip, making the figure commercially meaningful for fabless customers weighing foundry selection.

briefs.headline: Top-10 fabless IC designers post 73% revenue surge as AMD breaks into top three
briefs.paragraph: Combined revenue for the world's top-10 fabless IC design companies — firms that design chips but outsource manufacturing to foundries — surged **73% year over year** to more than $141.45 billion in Q2 2026, according to TrendForce, as AI demand lifted GPU, CPU, ASIC, and interconnect shipments across the board. AMD broke into the top three for the first time, displacing an incumbent. The figures translate directly into equipment demand: sustained fabless revenue growth at this scale underpins the capex (spending on new buildings and machines) commitments that drive WFE orders.

briefs.headline: Glass substrate supply stays tight as TGV metallization remains a key process hurdle
briefs.paragraph: Building on last week's report on Spirox's nonlinear-optical TGV inspection tool, supply-chain sources in Taiwan say low-CTE glass fiber cloth (used in high-end substrates to minimize thermal expansion mismatch) remains in short supply, while glass-core substrates for next-generation packaging are still in technical validation. The persistent bottleneck is **through-glass via metallization** — filling the vertical copper conductors drilled through glass panels consistently and reliably at production scale — alongside concerns about glass brittleness during handling. The global IC substrate market is separately forecast to grow 32% to $19.5 billion in 2026.

email_subject: High-NA EUV nears production ramp; EU updates dual-use controls; Mo EUV masks boost contrast 35%
intro: High-NA EUV is crossing from lab validation into early production economics, while the EU quietly updated its dual-use export control list and a NYCU/TSMC paper proposes a mask architecture that could extend 0.33-NA tools further than expected.

lead_brief.headline: High-NA EUV crosses into production ramp as economics become the gating factor
lead_brief.paragraph: **ASML** now has 10 High-NA EUV systems (next-gen EUV lithography tools with higher numerical aperture, which tightens the diffraction-limited resolution limit) running across four customer sites worldwide, with three additional units in shipment or installation — a threshold that moves the technology from laboratory validation into early production ramp. The physics case for High-NA has always been clear: a higher numerical aperture shrinks the minimum printable half-pitch proportionally, enabling the finer features required for sub-2nm logic and advanced DRAM. What has shifted is the question the industry is now asking — not whether the optics work, but whether the per-wafer cost can be justified against double- or multiple-patterning workarounds on existing 0.33-NA tools. Production adoption will therefore be paced by yield learning curves, resist compatibility (imec's chemically amplified resist work at 22nm pitch, reported at SPIE this week, is directly relevant here), and the photomask supply chain transitioning to larger 6×12-inch reticles. The three machines now being installed signal that at least one or two leading chipmakers have decided the economics clear the bar **for volume ramp**, though the broader industry timeline remains tied to cost-per-layer calculations rather than optical capability alone.

briefs.headline: EU updates dual-use export control list, adding semiconductor equipment items
briefs.paragraph: The **European Commission** adopted a Delegated Regulation on September 14 updating Annex I of the EU's dual-use export control framework — the list governing items that have both civilian and military applications, including advanced semiconductor manufacturing tools. The update follows similar moves by the US and the Netherlands and could affect equipment exports by European suppliers. Specific line items added were not detailed in the public notice, but the timing aligns with broader Western coordination on **restricting advanced chipmaking technology** transfers.

briefs.headline: Imec shows chemically amplified resists can print 22nm pitch under High-NA EUV
briefs.paragraph: At the SPIE Photomask Technology + EUV Lithography Conference this week, **imec** (Belgian R&D hub for chipmaking) demonstrated single-exposure patterning of random logic structures at 22nm pitch lines/spaces and 28nm center-to-center via arrays using conventional CAR (chemically amplified resist — a photosensitive polymer that reacts to EUV photons via acid catalysis) in a High-NA EUV step. The result matters because it suggests the industry's existing resist infrastructure can be extended into High-NA without an immediate forced switch to costlier next-generation resist chemistries, **reducing one adoption barrier** for early production customers.

briefs.headline: Molybdenum phase-only EUV masks deliver 35% higher image contrast at 12.5nm half-pitch
briefs.paragraph: Researchers at **National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University** and TSMC published simulation results showing that molybdenum-based quasi phase-only masks (photomasks that modulate the phase of reflected EUV light rather than absorbing it) outperform conventional tantalum absorber masks by a wide margin on the standard 0.33-NA EUV platform. The team reports **35% higher image contrast**, a fivefold increase in common focus window, and 92% lower peak telecentricity error, enabling 12.5nm half-pitch resolution with monopole illumination — all without changing the scanner hardware.

briefs.headline: Fujitsu's Monaka AI CPU targets 2027 mass production on TSMC 2nm
briefs.paragraph: **Fujitsu** plans to begin commercial sales of its Monaka AI CPU as early as 2027 in Japan, the US, and parts of Asia, manufactured on **TSMC** (Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, world's largest foundry) 2nm process. Monaka draws on design techniques developed for the Fugaku supercomputer and is positioned for AI inference workloads where power efficiency is a priority. The chip would be among the first commercial products to use TSMC's 2nm node (manufacturing generation) in volume, adding to the list of customers validating that process alongside Apple and Nvidia.

briefs.headline: Samsung and Qualcomm deepen 2nm talks as yield and pricing remain unresolved
briefs.paragraph: Ongoing negotiations between **Samsung** Electronics and Qualcomm over 2nm foundry production are expanding in scope, but pricing structures, yield targets, and process optimization details remain open — a recurring friction point as Samsung seeks to recapture flagship processor orders it lost to TSMC. The talks are running parallel to Samsung's broader effort to close the High-NA DRAM timeline gap with SK Hynix and to sign up design-tool partners, with **Qualcomm** representing a potentially large anchor customer that could validate Samsung's 2nm ramp economics.

briefs.headline: Samsung and SK Hynix reject $19 billion power prepayment as Korea expands chip infrastructure
briefs.paragraph: South Korea's push to accelerate semiconductor expansion hit a financing snag after **Samsung Electronics** and SK Hynix declined a government-backed proposal to prepay KRW 25 trillion (roughly US$18.7 billion) in future electricity bills — a mechanism designed to fund the grid upgrades that new fabs (chip factories) and their power-hungry AI workloads require. The rejection highlights a structural tension in Korea's chip buildout: chipmakers need reliable power infrastructure, but **neither company** is willing to effectively pre-fund state utility expansion on those terms.

briefs.headline: Co-packaged optics approach mass production as alignment and yield become the hard problems
briefs.paragraph: Co-packaged optics (CPO — integrating optical transceivers directly into the switch or processor package to cut latency and power) is moving toward mass production readiness, but the engineering challenges have shifted from optical engine performance to assembly precision, serviceability, and supply-chain coherence. Tight alignment tolerances between the photonic die and the electrical package, combined with the difficulty of replacing a failed optical engine in a deployed system, are now the gating issues. **Yield and interface standardization** across light sources, packaging, and test equipment remain unsolved at the volumes AI data-center buildouts will require.

briefs.headline: Semicon India 2026 exhibitor count nearly doubles, led by equipment and materials suppliers
briefs.paragraph: Exhibitor count at **Semicon India 2026** has reached 535 companies — up 52% from 2025 and 97% from 2024 — with the sharpest growth coming not from chip designers but from cleanroom contractors, specialty gas and chemical suppliers, and metrology and inspection tool vendors. That supplier-led composition signals that India's semiconductor buildout has moved from policy announcements into active procurement: companies invest in trade-show presence when purchasing decisions are real. The show opens in New Delhi on **September 17**, with the India semiconductor funding environment already at a multi-year high for deal volume.

email_subject: TSMC capacity stays tight; global semicon revenue hits $425B record; DRAM supply gap widens
intro: AI demand continues to reshape the semiconductor industry's supply picture. TSMC's most advanced nodes remain fully booked, a new record in global chip revenue confirms the cycle's strength, and memory makers are signaling a supply crunch into 2027-28.

lead_brief.headline: TSMC advanced capacity stays locked up as AWS and new customers join queue
lead_brief.paragraph: **TSMC** (Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, world's largest foundry — chip-for-hire factory) entered late Q3 2026 with its 3nm, 2nm, and CoWoS (chip-on-wafer-on-substrate — a 2.5D advanced packaging technology that stacks logic and memory side by side) capacity all in short supply. Nvidia and Apple continue to hold the largest claims on those resources, but AWS has recently expanded AI chip tape-outs through its Annapurna silicon design team, absorbing additional 3nm allocation. MediaTek and Google's TPU program have also shifted their capacity positions, prompting TSMC to actively rebalance its advanced-node scheduling. The situation reflects a broader supply constraint visible in the macro numbers: **global semiconductor revenue hit a record $425 billion in Q2 2026**, up 31.4% quarter over quarter according to Omdia — a growth rate that itself set a record. With leading-edge wafer starts sold out and CoWoS back-end packaging acting as a co-bottleneck, any new entrant seeking advanced capacity faces a queue measured in quarters rather than weeks.

briefs.headline: DRAM makers signal deep supply cuts through 2027 and 2028
briefs.paragraph: Memory suppliers have quietly notified module makers that shipment allocations will be **drastically cut in 2027**, with upstream manufacturers reportedly sold out through 2028 on long-term agreements. A separate forecast from Beijing-based Sigmaintell Consulting expects the supply-demand gap to narrow later in 2027 as new DRAM capacity comes online, but projects a potential demand pullback in 2029 as AI application patterns mature. The competing signals suggest module makers face near-term scarcity even as longer-cycle capacity investments eventually catch up.

briefs.headline: Chinese equipment makers reach 35% share in domestic fabs
briefs.paragraph: Domestic semiconductor equipment suppliers in China accounted for roughly **35% of tools installed** at Chinese fabs (chip factories) in 2025, up from about 25% the prior year, according to DIGITIMES supply-chain sources. The gain reflects accelerating substitution across etch, deposition, and cleaning tool categories as Chinese makers including AMEC expand their installed base amid sustained Western export controls (US/Dutch/Japanese rules restricting equipment sales to China). The trajectory suggests Chinese domestic equipment share could approach or exceed 40% within the next year if current trends hold.

briefs.headline: Kioxia weighs $10 billion US stock listing for 2027
briefs.paragraph: **Kioxia**, the Tokyo-based NAND flash and SSD maker spun out of Toshiba's memory division, is in early discussions with Bank of America, Goldman Sachs, and JPMorgan Chase about a US initial public offering that could raise roughly **$10 billion** in 2027, according to Bloomberg. A US listing would give Kioxia access to deeper capital markets as it competes with Samsung and SK Hynix in a memory cycle that is tightening through at least 2028. No timeline or exchange has been formally announced.

briefs.headline: Silicon photonics substrate supply emerges as next optical module bottleneck
briefs.paragraph: The data-center optical module market is projected to grow from $12.6 billion in 2025 to $45.4 billion by 2030, driven by silicon photonics (SiPh — integrating optical functions onto a silicon chip using standard fab processes) at 800G and above. Volume shipments of 1.6 terabit-per-second modules are set to scale in 2026, with 3.2T modules contributing revenue by 2028. The binding constraint has shifted upstream: laser-grade indium phosphide substrates used in SiPh light sources are now the supply bottleneck, not device manufacturing capacity itself.

briefs.headline: Murata eyes larger MLCC capacity expansion as AI server demand holds past 2028
briefs.paragraph: **Murata Manufacturing** is evaluating a new and potentially larger round of multilayer ceramic capacitor (MLCC — tiny passive components used by the hundreds per server board) capacity expansion, beyond investment plans already underway, as AI server demand projections now extend firmly past 2028. MLCCs are passive components whose volumes scale with server board complexity, so sustained AI infrastructure buildout directly translates to **multi-year capacity pressure** for Murata and its peers.

briefs.headline: MIRTEC debuts hybrid 3D inspection system combining Moiré and laser scanning
briefs.paragraph: **MIRTEC** is showcasing its MV-9SiP Hybrid 3D Inspection System at SEMICON West 2026, combining three measurement modalities in a single platform: conventional 2D machine vision, 12-projection digital blue-light Moiré fringe projection (which extracts height maps by analyzing deformation of projected fringe patterns), and blue laser point-cloud scanning. Integrating all three in one tool lets fabs (chip factories) cross-validate height and coplanarity measurements on system-in-package assemblies **without moving the part between stations**, reducing handling risk and cycle time.

briefs.headline: Teradyne opens Bengaluru office to support India chip ecosystem growth
briefs.paragraph: **Teradyne**, the US semiconductor test equipment maker, has opened an office in Bengaluru to provide local customer support, applications engineering, and training as India's chip design and manufacturing base expands. The move follows the broader wave of equipment and materials suppliers establishing India presence — a trend this digest tracked through Semicon India 2026's **near-doubling of exhibitor count**. Teradyne's Bengaluru hub will focus on engaging chipmakers and electronics manufacturers already active in the region.

email_subject: SK Hynix eyes Intel Ohio for US HBM output; HBM base die sourcing reshapes memory supply chain; Kepler bets on EUV-free stacking
intro: Memory supply-chain geography is shifting fast: SK Hynix is in talks to manufacture HBM on US soil, Samsung is tapping TSMC for base dies, and a stealthy startup claims it can scale HBM without EUV at all.

lead_brief.headline: SK Hynix and Intel in talks to manufacture HBM inside the United States
lead_brief.paragraph: **SK Hynix** — South Korea's second-largest memory chipmaker and the dominant supplier of high-bandwidth memory (HBM — stacked DRAM dies used in AI accelerators) — is in active discussions with **Intel** about establishing its first US memory manufacturing operation, according to multiple reports. Two structures are on the table: leasing space inside Intel's existing fab (chip factory) in Ohio, or forming a joint venture that would also include cloud hyperscalers seeking a secure domestic supply. The talks come as HBM supply remains extremely tight and as US-South Korea trade negotiations add political urgency to onshoring memory production. The Ohio Intel site is a natural candidate because it already has advanced process infrastructure, reducing the time and capital needed to qualify a new facility. Separately, the same reports note that SK Hynix is weighing Intel as an additional foundry source for HBM base dies — the logic die at the bottom of each HBM stack that routes data between memory layers and the host processor — beginning with the HBM4E generation, though one analysis flags that Intel may not hold a cost advantage over TSMC for that work. Neither company has confirmed the talks.

briefs.headline: HBM base die sourcing becomes a multi-vendor contest as Samsung taps TSMC
briefs.paragraph: The logic die at the base of every HBM stack has quietly become a new competitive front. **TSMC** (Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, world's largest foundry — chip-for-hire factory) is now reportedly manufacturing custom base dies for Samsung Electronics, while Micron has confirmed TSMC will build its next-generation base die too. That leaves SK Hynix as the outlier still weighing its options — Intel alongside TSMC — and signals that **single-vendor base-die supply is ending** across the industry.

briefs.headline: Kepler Computing claims HBM can scale to next generation without EUV
briefs.paragraph: Seven years after founding, memory startup **Kepler Computing** has emerged from stealth with $468 million in total funding and a claim that high-bandwidth memory can be scaled to the next density tier **without EUV** (extreme ultraviolet, 13.5 nm lithography — the most advanced chip-printing process). Kepler reportedly upgraded a GlobalFoundries fab in eight months and has secured commitments from major chip customers, directly challenging the assumption that future HBM generations require EUV patterning.

briefs.headline: Memory makers post triple-digit revenue growth; Samsung outsources DDR5 to protect HBM capacity
briefs.paragraph: Major memory suppliers posted record revenue in Q2 2026, with year-over-year growth remaining in triple digits, driven by AI server demand. **Samsung Electronics** is responding by pushing all additional DDR5 module production to outside assemblers — OSAT (outsourced semiconductor assembly and test) partners in Vietnam, India, and the Philippines — **reserving its own back-end capacity entirely for HBM**. SK Hynix's move toward US production adds another dimension to how all three leading suppliers are reshaping their manufacturing footprints.

briefs.headline: Glass substrates and through-glass vias draw new equipment entrants ahead of 2027
briefs.paragraph: Glass substrate technology — where through-glass vias (TGVs — vertical electrical connections drilled through glass panels) replace conventional organic laminate interposers for tighter chip-to-chip interconnects — is attracting new equipment and materials players ahead of projected 2027 volume ramp. **SUSS MicroTec** announced a €45 million advanced packaging innovation center in Germany focused on next-generation process solutions. Separately, Fu Chun Shin Machinery teamed with Korean-Chinese joint venture Zhongke Xianfeng on TGV drilling equipment, while startup Geckos is promoting a copper-paste vacuum-printing process as a lower-cost via-fill alternative for denser interconnects.

briefs.headline: DUV resist bake conditions found to drive stochastic defects at advanced nodes
briefs.paragraph: A study published on SemiWiki examines how post-apply bake (PAB) and post-exposure bake (PEB) conditions in chemically amplified photoresists affect stochastic patterning failures in **193 nm ArF immersion DUV** (deep-ultraviolet — the older 193 nm chip-printing workhorse, still critical for most layers). Bake temperature, duration, and wafer-temperature uniformity all influence critical dimension, line-edge roughness, and local CD uniformity — meaning that **thermal processing, not just photon shot noise**, governs defect probability at the smallest features. The findings are relevant to any fab still relying on DUV for leading-edge multi-patterning layers.

briefs.headline: Jensen Huang says China will build advanced lithography tools by 2030
briefs.paragraph: **Nvidia** CEO Jensen Huang said publicly that China will develop its own advanced semiconductor lithography (the chip-printing optical process) equipment by 2030, describing the achievement as **

briefs.headline: MediaTek ships first 2nm mobile SoC; CPO scaling hits fiber assembly wall
briefs.paragraph: **MediaTek** launched the Dimensity 9600 Pro, the first smartphone system-on-chip built on TSMC's 2nm process node — adding to Fujitsu's Monaka CPU reported last week as early commercial 2nm volume. On the optical interconnect side, BizLink has begun small-volume shipments of co-packaged optics (CPO — optical transceivers integrated directly into the switch package), but its chairman flagged that **fiber array unit assembly**, thermal management, and system reliability — not production capacity — are the binding constraints on mass deployment, consistent with last week's broader CPO ramp coverage.

briefs.headline: Gradiant lands $300 million in ultrapure water contracts at US chip fabs
briefs.paragraph: **Gradiant**, a water treatment specialist, has won **$300 million** in new contracts to supply ultrapure water, wastewater treatment, and zero liquid discharge systems at semiconductor fabs in New York, Virginia, Idaho, and Utah. The wins reflect the scale of water infrastructure required as US chip manufacturing expands under CHIPS Act (2022 US semiconductor manufacturing subsidy law) investment — ultrapure water consumption at a leading-edge fab can run to millions of gallons per day and is a prerequisite for any advanced process line.

email_subject: China plots DUV path to 3nm GAA; Lam and AMAT commit $1.4B to India; memory LTAs lock up 70% of capacity
intro: China's Academy of Sciences has mapped a gate-all-around process route below 3nm that skips EUV entirely, while US equipment giants pour over a billion dollars into India ahead of SEMICON. Memory suppliers, meanwhile, are locking up the majority of capacity in long-term contracts as 2027 supply tightens.

lead_brief.headline: China's CAS maps gate-all-around process route to 3nm without EUV
lead_brief.paragraph: China's Institute of Microelectronics of the **Chinese Academy of Sciences** has established a gate-all-around (GAA — a transistor geometry where the gate wraps fully around the channel, enabling better electrostatic control at sub-5nm scales) device development path to process nodes below 3nm using DUV (deep ultraviolet, 193nm wavelength) lithography rather than EUV. This is technically ambitious because EUV's 13.5nm wavelength prints features that DUV at 193nm cannot resolve in a single exposure — DUV-based approaches must compensate through multi-patterning (printing the same layer in two or more sequential exposures with tight overlay), aggressive optical proximity correction, and process-tuning of the resist and etch steps. GAA nanosheets also impose their own patterning demands: the channel stack requires precision fin definition and selective etching that EUV normally simplifies. The CAS route would need to close that gap entirely through process chemistry and multi-patterning discipline. No specific resolution or overlay figures were disclosed, but the roadmap signals that China's domestic research institutions are pursuing **a parallel scaling path** that sidesteps the export-controlled EUV tools they cannot currently obtain.

briefs.headline: Lam Research and Applied Materials together pledge $1.4 billion for India expansion
briefs.paragraph: Timed to SEMICON India 2026, **Lam Research** (US wafer-fab equipment specialist in etch and deposition) announced roughly $1.04 billion in India investment to build its first silicon component manufacturing facility in the country and expand R&D. **Applied Materials** separately committed $375 million over ten years in Karnataka, targeting around 1,000 new jobs. Fujifilm added an $83 million semiconductor materials plant, bringing the combined three-day pre-show total to **$1.5 billion** across equipment and process chemicals.

briefs.headline: Memory suppliers locking 50-70% of output into long-term supply agreements
briefs.paragraph: The memory supply squeeze is reshaping how capacity gets allocated. **Kioxia** has committed roughly 50% of its output to long-term supply agreements (LTAs — multi-year contracts that pre-commit production capacity), while South Korea's two major vendors — Samsung and SK Hynix — reserve about 70% under similar deals, and Micron around 60%. Contract durations are stretching from three years to five as customers try to secure supply through what many expect to be **the tightest year yet** for memory in 2027.

briefs.headline: Twenty Chinese OSATs push into advanced packaging as EUV restrictions persist
briefs.paragraph: Restricted from obtaining leading-edge EUV lithography tools, Chinese chipmakers are accelerating a packaging-driven scaling strategy. **Twenty OSATs** (outsourced semiconductor assembly and test — companies that package and test finished chips) are now pushing into advanced packaging, expanding well beyond China's largest assembly houses to include specialist packaging firms and chiplet startups targeting AI and high-performance computing. The shift mirrors the broader domestic playbook of routing around process-node limitations through 3D integration and chiplet disaggregation.

briefs.headline: Synopsys simulation predicted High-NA EUV line-edge roughness asymmetry four years early
briefs.paragraph: A **Synopsys** S-Litho optical simulation run in 2021 predicted that vertical lines in 22nm-pitch High-NA EUV patterning would show worse line-edge roughness (LER — the deviation of a printed edge from its intended path, measured in nanometers) than horizontal lines — reversing the behavior seen in conventional lower-NA EUV. IBM's actual 21nm silicon results, presented at conferences in 2025 and 2026, confirmed **the 0.3nm LER difference** between orientations that the model had forecast. The result demonstrates that pre-silicon optical simulation can catch asymmetric resist and diffraction effects years before wafer hardware is available.

briefs.headline: Google's 2027 TPU weighs CoWoS backup as Intel EMIB-T substrate yields stabilize
briefs.paragraph: **Google**'s Humufish TPU, targeting mass production by end of 2027, is designed around Intel's EMIB-T (Embedded Multi-die Interconnect Bridge — Tilted, an advanced substrate that routes signals between chiplets at short range) advanced packaging with ASIC support from MediaTek. MediaTek indicated during an earnings call that EMIB-T yields have reached levels capable of stable mass production. Google is nonetheless evaluating **CoWoS** (chip-on-wafer-on-substrate — TSMC's interposer-based multi-chip packaging) as a contingency if substrate supply falters heading into the production ramp.

briefs.headline: SK Hynix-Intel Ohio talks continue as geopolitical logic drives the deal
briefs.paragraph: Negotiations between **SK Hynix** and Intel over possible use of Intel's Ohio fab (chip factory) for US-based memory production are continuing, with analysts at EE Times noting the primary driver is geopolitical rather than purely technical — Washington is pressing memory suppliers to establish domestic manufacturing. The arrangement would give SK Hynix **its first US memory production site**, while potentially giving Intel's underutilized Ohio facility a revenue-generating tenant. Pricing and operational structure remain unsettled.

briefs.headline: Dutch cabinet proposes multi-billion-euro innovation funding package inspired by DARPA
briefs.paragraph: The Dutch cabinet has proposed a funding package that includes €500 million for a new National Agency for Disruptive Innovation (NADI), €333 million to revive the National Growth Fund through 2031, and a **€3.5 billion public investment institution** targeting digitalization, AI, energy, and life sciences. The NADI concept was put forward by former ASML CEO Peter Wennink in a report on Dutch economic competitiveness and is modeled on the US DARPA structure, funding consortia of companies, startups, and universities on major technological challenges.

briefs.headline: Micron launches 512GB DDR5-9200 modules, challenging Samsung's five-year lead
briefs.paragraph: **Micron** has announced 512GB DDR5-9200 memory modules drawing just 16 watts each — the first direct rival to Samsung's 512GB DDR5 modules after a five-year gap at the top of the market. Servers can be configured with **up to 12TB** per system using these modules, and Micron claims the design is 60% less energy-intensive than running four 128GB modules to reach the same capacity. Speed bins go up to 9200 MT/s, though module pricing is expected to remain steep even for hyperscale buyers.

email_subject: High-NA EUV wins over TSMC, Samsung, SK Hynix; EU tightens export controls; Winbond buys Infineon NOR unit
intro: High-NA EUV adoption is broadening from Intel's early lead to a full-industry commitment — the biggest structural story in chipmaking equipment this cycle. Elsewhere, export-control tightening and a $1.12 billion NOR flash acquisition round out a busy day.

lead_brief.headline: High-NA EUV moves from Intel test bed to full-industry adoption roadmap
lead_brief.paragraph: **ASML**'s High-NA EUV platform — which raises the projection lens numerical aperture (NA, a dimensionless measure of the light cone angle that directly sets the minimum printable feature size) from 0.33 to 0.55 — is winning commitments across all four leading chipmakers. The higher NA delivers roughly 40% smaller features than current EUV systems, enough to replace multiple patterning steps (where a layer is exposed several times with shifted masks to achieve finer pitch) with a single exposure, cutting process complexity and potential defect accumulation. Intel Foundry moved first: ASML confirmed in July that Intel had put High-NA into selected layers of its 18A logic node for Panther Lake processors, **processing more than one million wafers** across research, qualification, and production runs — the first high-volume logic product made with the technology, with yields matching Intel's established EUV baseline. Samsung is targeting High-NA for DRAM production by 2028, SK Hynix around the same period, and TSMC — which had questioned cost justification — now expects deployment by 2030. One optical constraint remains: the anamorphic lens design exposes only half the field area of existing EUV systems, which forces designers of large AI accelerators to stitch multiple exposures together, adding alignment overhead and yield risk. Each tool costs roughly $400 million, about twice a conventional EUV system, yet the breadth of customer timelines now substantially de-risks High-NA as a platform.

briefs.headline: EU tightens export controls on dual-use high-tech goods
briefs.paragraph: The **European Union** has tightened export controls on high-tech goods with potential military applications, extending restrictions beyond semiconductors to a broader set of dual-use technologies. The move follows parallel tightening by the US and Dutch governments and adds another layer of compliance overhead for equipment makers shipping to sensitive destinations. Combined with ongoing US and Dutch controls on advanced lithography and related tools, the action continues **narrowing legal export channels** for leading-edge semiconductor equipment globally.

briefs.headline: Winbond acquires Infineon NOR flash unit for $1.12 billion
briefs.paragraph: **Winbond** Electronics has agreed to pay $1.12 billion in cash for Infineon Technologies' NOR flash and F-RAM businesses, **vaulting it to the top of the automotive NOR market** while adding server and AI data-center supply positions. NOR flash (a non-volatile memory type used for firmware storage, distinct from NAND's bulk data role) has seen tightening supply as AI servers multiply the number of chips requiring boot storage. The deal consolidates a market segment that had been split among several mid-tier suppliers.

briefs.headline: Chip equipment makers waiting up to 40 months for critical parts
briefs.paragraph: Delivery times for specialized components used in semiconductor capital equipment have stretched to **as long as 40 months**, according to Digitimes, as chipmakers accelerate fab investment faster than the equipment supply chain can respond. The shortage sits one tier below the headline tool makers — in the precision castings, custom optics, high-vacuum hardware, and motion stages that go into the tools themselves — and could delay fab ramp schedules even where equipment orders are fully funded.

briefs.headline: ASML stays with laser-plasma EUV sources, dismisses free-electron laser alternative
briefs.paragraph: **ASML** is doubling down on laser-produced plasma (LPP — where a high-power CO₂ laser vaporizes tin droplets to generate 13.5 nm EUV light) as its light-source roadmap, targeting **1,000-watt output** from its next-generation LPP systems. The company is not pursuing free-electron laser (FEL) technology — backed in part by Elon Musk — which uses a particle accelerator to generate tunable X-ray or EUV light. ASML's position reflects confidence that LPP can deliver the source power needed for High-NA throughput without the physical footprint and capital cost a particle accelerator would require.

briefs.headline: Applied Materials raises India commitment to $5 billion through 2035
briefs.paragraph: Following last week's Lam Research and Applied Materials pledges at SEMICON India 2026, **Applied Materials** has now specified its commitment at $5 billion through 2035 — the updated figure includes a 140-acre advanced semiconductor research park and expanded domestic supply-chain development. As a broader Digitimes analysis notes, multinationals filling Semicon India 2026 committed **to every layer except fabs**: equipment manufacturing, materials, assembly and test, and design centers rather than front-end wafer fabrication, which remains the gap in India's ambitions under its $13.5 billion Semicon 2.0 program.

briefs.headline: CoWoS-L expected to dominate AI chip packaging through 2028
briefs.paragraph: **TrendForce** forecasts that TSMC's CoWoS-L (chip-on-wafer-on-substrate with a larger interposer — the silicon bridge layer connecting multiple dies in a 2.5D package) will remain the mainstream advanced packaging solution for AI chips through 2028, despite competition from Intel's EMIB-T. GPU suppliers and hyperscale cloud providers are pushing package sizes beyond single reticle limits, making interposer area the binding constraint. CoWoS-L's advantages in **technology maturity and yield** are expected to outweigh EMIB-T's cost profile over that horizon.

briefs.headline: Resonac grows first 300mm silicon carbide crystal
briefs.paragraph: **Resonac** has grown and processed a 300mm silicon carbide (SiC) single crystal — a substrate milestone for power electronics used in electric vehicles and data centers. Current SiC production runs on 150mm and 200mm wafers; moving to 300mm (the standard diameter for leading-edge silicon fabs) would let manufacturers use existing 300mm tooling and **sharply cut per-die cost** through larger wafer area. Growing defect-free SiC boules at this diameter has been a long-standing materials challenge because SiC crystallizes at extremely high temperatures with strong tendencies toward polytypic defects.

briefs.headline: US awards $1 billion to Anderon for domestic quantum wafer production
briefs.paragraph: The US government has awarded **$1 billion** to Anderon — an IBM-backed venture — to establish quantum wafer manufacturing on US soil. Quantum processors require wafers with extreme purity and specialized superconducting films (typically aluminum or niobium deposited on silicon or sapphire substrates) processed in conditions far more demanding than conventional CMOS. The award signals Washington's intent to **secure a domestic quantum fabrication base** as the technology moves from laboratory demonstration toward early commercial deployment, following the pattern of CHIPS Act investments in classical semiconductor manufacturing.

email_subject: Intel puts High-NA EUV into production; CXMT claims 5th-gen DRAM; TSMC CoWoS to double
intro: Intel's Panther Lake chip has become the first commercial product to use High-NA EUV in volume manufacturing, a milestone the industry has been tracking for years. Meanwhile China's CXMT claims a generational leap in DRAM, and TSMC's advanced packaging capacity is set to double.

lead_brief.headline: Intel validates High-NA EUV in production with Panther Lake chip
lead_brief.paragraph: **Intel** has moved High-NA EUV (extreme ultraviolet lithography with a higher numerical aperture projection lens, which tightens the minimum printable feature size) into full manufacturing on its Panther Lake processor — **the first commercial product** to do so. The higher NA increases the sine of the maximum light-cone half-angle collected by the lens, directly shrinking the diffraction-limited resolution limit; more of the available spatial frequencies from the mask reach the wafer, enabling smaller, denser features without multiple patterning at the same pitch. Stitching, however, remains an unresolved production challenge: High-NA's smaller exposure field means large dies must be printed in two or more overlapping exposures and electrically joined at the seam, and the EE Times report notes that the yield and reliability of those stitched interconnects have not yet been fully demonstrated at scale. Larger mask sizes — which would restore field area and reduce or eliminate stitching — are on the roadmap but not yet in production. Intel's validation confirms the tool can print at production quality, but the stitching question will determine how quickly the rest of the industry follows with full-reticle designs.

briefs.headline: CXMT claims fifth-generation DRAM platform enters mass production
briefs.paragraph: China's **CXMT** (ChangXin Memory Technologies, China's leading DRAM maker) says its fifth-generation process platform — the G5 — has entered mass production, bringing LPDDR5X (low-power double-data-rate 5X mobile memory) into volume output at density levels it claims are comparable to the industry's current leading nodes. If verified, **this closes the gap** with Samsung and SK Hynix significantly. CXMT is also separately reported to be planning a 3D NAND research and pilot line at a second fab near Beijing, signaling ambitions beyond DRAM.

briefs.headline: TSMC CoWoS capacity set to double by 2028 as AI packaging demand hardens
briefs.paragraph: Updating last week's CoWoS-L coverage: **TSMC** is reportedly planning to double its CoWoS (chip-on-wafer-on-substrate, a 2.5D packaging technology connecting dies via a silicon interposer) capacity from roughly 130,000 300mm-equivalent wafers per month at end-2026 to 260,000 by 2028. The expansion tracks AI infrastructure demand hardening into a multiyear cycle rather than a temporary spike. Even so, larger multi-die packages mean **doubling capacity won't double accelerator output** — each package consumes more interposer area, and HBM availability, substrate supply, and test capacity remain independent bottlenecks.

briefs.headline: Samsung forms dedicated robotics team to automate fab maintenance
briefs.paragraph: **Samsung Electronics** has created a dedicated internal organization to develop and deploy robots inside its semiconductor fabs (chip factories), with equipment preventive maintenance — the regular inspection and servicing that currently relies heavily on engineers — identified as the first target. The move reflects both labor-cost pressure and the difficulty of staffing highly specialized maintenance roles at scale. Automating PM cycles could also **reduce tool downtime**, a meaningful lever when a single idle EUV scanner can cost millions of dollars per day in lost output.

briefs.headline: Solidigm weighs first US NAND plant as domestic flash supply draws attention
briefs.paragraph: **Solidigm**, the NAND flash subsidiary of SK Hynix, is evaluating sites in the eastern United States for its **first US-based NAND mass-production line**. The review is still in early stages, with no site selected. The consideration comes as US policy pressure mounts on memory supply chains and as SK Hynix separately continues talks with Intel over potential US-based HBM production at Intel's Ohio fab — a thread this digest has followed over the past week.

briefs.headline: ByteDance substrate crunch highlights China AI packaging bottleneck
briefs.paragraph: China's AI buildout is running into a substrate supply wall. **ByteDance** is reportedly planning to spend CNY 100 billion (roughly US$14.9 billion) per year on advanced packaging substrates by 2030, joining Huawei HiSilicon, Hygon, and major OSATs (outsourced chip assembly and test houses) in a scramble for high-end capacity. Digitimes Intelligence separately notes that the substrate equipment bottleneck has **shifted from upstream materials to tooling**, as larger, higher-layer-count substrates for AI accelerators push beyond what existing lamination and plating equipment can handle.

briefs.headline: GlobalFoundries and Marvell expand SiGe deal for AI optical interconnects
briefs.paragraph: **GlobalFoundries** and **Marvell** have signed a multi-year strategic agreement to expand capacity for silicon-germanium (SiGe — a compound semiconductor process used to build high-speed analog and RF circuits) technology. The partnership targets AI data-center optical connectivity, where SiGe transistors enable the high-frequency transceiver circuits that drive co-packaged optics and coherent links. Separately, Dutch research institute **TNO** announced plans to potentially double output at its indium-phosphide photonic chip pilot plant in Eindhoven — from 10,000 to 20,000 six-inch wafers per year — as photonics demand from AI data centers accelerates.

briefs.headline: Taiwan chip test equipment leads sector growth; NOR flash faces severe undersupply
briefs.paragraph: Two-thirds of Taiwan's listed semiconductor equipment and components revenue growth traces to a single process step: **chip testing**, driven by AI chip complexity and the need to verify multi-die packages before shipping, according to Digitimes. In a parallel squeeze, NOR flash and SLC NAND — the simpler memory types used in everyday electronics — face **severe undersupply** as fabs route capacity toward higher-margin DRAM and 3D NAND for AI servers, threatening supply for automotive and industrial customers.

email_subject: DRAM value tops leading-edge logic; TSMC-ASE break ground in Kaohsiung; CXMT 12nm update
intro: AI demand is reshuffling memory economics at the wafer level, while advanced packaging capacity takes a concrete step forward in Taiwan. CXMT's fifth-generation DRAM process also draws new technical scrutiny.

lead_brief.headline: DRAM wafer value now exceeds leading-edge logic on per-area basis
lead_brief.paragraph: AI-driven demand has pushed DRAM economics past a threshold that would have seemed implausible a few years ago: DRAM makers are now extracting more revenue per unit of silicon area than **TSMC** collects for its most advanced N3 (3-nanometer-class) logic wafers. The shift reflects two converging forces. On the demand side, AI training and inference workloads require massive, high-bandwidth memory — HBM stacks in particular — and suppliers have concentrated shipments under long-term agreements that lock in 50–70% of output, tightening spot availability and pushing contract prices up sharply. On the supply side, DRAM scaling is genuinely difficult: each new generation requires more lithography passes and tighter overlay (layer-to-layer alignment, in nanometers) than the last, and CXMT's new fifth-generation 12nm-class process relies on quadruple patterning — four sequential exposure steps to define a single feature pitch — **boosting die capacity by 50%** but at significant process complexity and cost. The TrendForce aggregate confirms the macro: global DRAM module revenue hit $21.2 billion in 2025, up 59% year over year, a dramatic acceleration from 7% growth in 2024. Samsung is now weighing a 4nm foundry expansion specifically to serve HBM4 base-die demand, with a 2nm line under review for future HBM5.

briefs.headline: TSMC and ASE break ground on Kaohsiung advanced packaging cluster
briefs.paragraph: Continuing the CoWoS expansion thread: **TSMC** and ASE Group have formally broken ground on Taiwan's first advanced packaging supply-chain cluster at Baipu Industrial Park in Kaohsiung. More than 20 companies attended the September 21 ceremony, including Foxconn. The first phase is already fully allocated — a sign that AI and high-performance computing demand is absorbing capacity as fast as it is built. The Kaohsiung site complements TSMC's broader plan to double CoWoS capacity by 2028.

briefs.headline: GlobalFoundries and Smart Photonics launch indium phosphide plus silicon photonics service
briefs.paragraph: **GlobalFoundries** and Eindhoven-based Smart Photonics have launched what they describe as the industry's first commercial open-access foundry service combining silicon photonics and indium phosphide (InP — a compound semiconductor needed for active optical components like lasers, modulators, and amplifiers that silicon cannot provide on its own). Smart Photonics' InP active components are integrated into cavities in the silicon chips via flip-chip bonding. General availability is targeted for the second half of 2027, with AI data centers, optical transceivers, and lidar as the primary markets.

briefs.headline: ASM launches flowable carbon material to simplify advanced patterning
briefs.paragraph: **ASM International** has introduced XP8 Vertos Flowable Carbon, a new hard-mask material aimed at collapsing the multi-step fill, planarization, and patterning sequences used in advanced logic and memory manufacturing. Conventional approaches treat gap-fill (flowing material into narrow trenches) and planarization (leveling the surface) as separate process steps; flowable carbon handles both in a single integrated pass, reducing defect opportunities and tightening topography control. ASM says the material targets **high-aspect-ratio structures** in DRAM and 3D NAND as well as advanced packaging applications.

briefs.headline: ASML opens India office, but scale-up waits on Tata's Dholera fab
briefs.paragraph: **ASML** has begun India operations with an initial team of 20–30 engineering graduates, keeping its footprint deliberately small for now. The company has signaled that any meaningful expansion is contingent on Tata Electronics delivering India's first 12-inch wafer fab (chip factory using 300mm silicon discs) at Dholera on schedule. The conditional stance underscores a pattern seen across the equipment industry: vendor investment in a new geography tracks fab construction milestones rather than leading them.

briefs.headline: Korean inspection equipment maker MIT files for Kosdaq listing
briefs.paragraph: South Korean semiconductor inspection and metrology equipment maker **MIT** has filed for a preliminary review with the Korea Exchange for a Kosdaq listing, with Samsung Securities as lead underwriter under a technology-based special listing program. MIT's focus on in-line defect detection and measurement tools puts it in a segment that has seen strong demand as chip geometries shrink and **process margin** — the window between a working and failing device — narrows at each new node.

briefs.headline: JNTC commits 347 billion won to through-glass via substrate plant
briefs.paragraph: South Korean materials company **JNTC** will invest 347 billion won (roughly $250 million) to build a through-glass via (TGV — vertical electrical connections etched through glass panels, analogous to the through-silicon vias used in chip stacking) substrate plant in Gimcheon. Glass substrates are attracting investment across the industry as an alternative to organic laminates for AI and high-performance computing packages, where their dimensional stability and finer redistribution-layer geometry are advantageous. A separate Korean components maker, EST, also filed for a **Kosdaq IPO** targeting glass substrates and micro-display applications.

briefs.headline: China GAA transistors without EUV face long road to a full node
briefs.paragraph: Following last week's coverage of IMECAS's gate-all-around demonstration: Tom's Hardware adds context that while China's Institute of Microelectronics has shown working GAA (gate-all-around — a transistor structure where the gate wraps fully around the channel, enabling denser, lower-power devices) stacked-nanosheet devices at 3nm-class dimensions using only DUV (193 nm) lithography with multiple patterning, the gap between a research transistor and **a manufacturable process node** remains years wide. Yield, interconnect density, and process integration at volume are the outstanding challenges.
